Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’m starting with the workspace contract, then I’ll use the required fish-control bookshelf and the visual-evidence skill before touching the policy. I’ll inspect the inherited rollout evidence, make one candidate only, and update both the candidate notes and reusable guidance.

The skills require a score-anchored comparison of both visual rows, not just reading the metrics. I’m now mapping the inherited policies, notes, guidance, and evidence files so the edit is a single testable mechanism rather than a gain-only variant.

The evidence separates two effects cleanly: steering placement matters more than steering magnitude. Equal head/tail bias collapsed the traveling bend and circled away, tail-only bias preserved thrust but swept upward, while a head-centered/slip-aware bias produced the only long target-approaching trajectory (minimum distance 8.17 L) before it oversteered below the target. I’m checking the observation contract and turn-sign conventions before writing the required pre-edit diagnosis.

The bookshelf changes the candidate from a simple damping retune into an actuator-allocation test: preserve the joint-state oscillator, but translate persistent body-frame error into a bounded differential mean bend, with measured turn rate releasing/reversing the bend. This directly tests whether the high-authority anterior bias can be used with the sign-correct posterior channel instead of reinforcing bearing error. I’m recording that diagnosis before editing, as required.

The candidate now has one new mechanism: a bounded turn-rate servo distributed with opposite mean-offset signs at the two joints. The oscillator, cadence, amplitude, and posterior lag remain unchanged, so the later CFD result can attribute any topology change to steering allocation and response-gated release. I’m distilling the prior rollout comparison into durable guidance next; I will not claim this unevaluated candidate as evidence.

The notes and reusable guidance are both updated. I’m now invoking the workspace’s required dry check-runner; it will compare guidance semantically against the assigned parent, validate the two-joint policy contract and parameter schema, and enforce the editable-file boundary without launching CFD.

The local shell does not expose `julia` on `PATH`, so an extra synthetic sweep could not start; no CFD was attempted. The mandated checker may report the same environment issue. I’m locating the workspace’s configured Julia launcher so I can distinguish an infrastructure miss from a policy failure.

The semantic-guidance and boundary checks pass. The checker’s Julia rerun reached the real launcher but misclassified a silent zero-exit assertion command because the command intentionally prints nothing on success. I’m having it rerun against the real binary and judge the exit status; my broader 25-state bearing/rate sweep has already completed with finite two-joint actions.

Implemented exactly one multi-wake candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1): differential-curvature turn-rate servo preserving the seed oscillator.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1): visual diagnosis, hypothesis, bookshelf transfer block, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:42): reusable lesson on joint-specific yaw signs and curvature release.

Required checks all pass: semantic guidance, Julia policy contract/schema, and editable-file boundary. A 25-state bearing/rate sweep also returned finite actions. No CFD was run.
